pullQuote.title: As good as it looks
pullQuote.quote: First mallet I've owned and I love it. Great feel, great touch. Looks amazing, people definitely notice and my longer putts outside of 5 feet have gotten better.

buyBody: You use it twice a hole and think about it least, and it decides more of your score than anything else you carry. The Tracer is milled from a single block of 304 stainless, so it comes off the face muted and solid with nothing inside to ring, with a slight toe hang that works with a natural arc instead of fighting it and the weight pushed out to the edges so an off-center strike holds its line. Right or left hand, sixty days to decide.

four.v: Plumber neck, for a natural arc

whatYouGet: One Tracer LGP02 Mallet putter in the hand you picked
Oversized 3.0 white and gold Lucky putter grip, fitted
No headcover (none of our clubs ship with one)
carePara: The gold is a finish, not a coating that needs babying, but the face still wants wiping after a wet round so the ball comes off it the same way every time.
The grip is white. Reviewers have flagged that it picks up dirt quickly. A wipe with a damp cloth after a round keeps it looking new for a lot longer than it otherwise would.
clubHeadline: The club you use most, thought about least. Lag it close and walk it in.
clubParas: Nobody buys a putter for the reason they should. A driver gets picked over three weekends and a putter gets whatever was in the bag when you started, and it is the club you use on every hole, twice, deciding more of your score than anything else you carry. The Tracer is milled from one block of 304 stainless, which is why it comes off the face muted and solid instead of ringing, and why a strike off the toe reads as information rather than a punishment.

clubSpecs.v: Mallet putter, CNC-milled from a single block of 304 stainless.
Muted and solid at impact, stable through the stroke, and easy to swing on its own arc.
One-piece 304 stainless head, milled face, 3.5° of loft and 365 g at 35 inches. Plumber neck, slight toe hang, gold finish, oversized 3.0 grip fitted.
Any golfer with a natural arc who would rather the head covered a miss than reported it.

helpPick.headline: Both suit an arc. The question is feel or forgiveness.
helpPick.sub: This is the only question worth asking about a putter and the usual answer (mallets for straight strokes, blades for arcs) does not apply here. Both Tracers are built for a stroke with a natural arc. What separates them is how much the head helps you on the ones you miss, and how much it tells you about them.

options.name: Tracer Mallet
options.body: Slight toe hang from a plumber neck, so it works with the arc you already have. Perimeter weighting keeps an off-center strike on line. You give up some feedback to get that.

options.name: Tracer Blade
options.body: For players who release the head through the stroke. Twenty grams heavier and far less forgiving, which is the trade: a blade tells you exactly where on the face you hit it.

helpPick.note: The blade is out of stock and right hand only when it returns. If you want the feedback rather than the forgiveness, that is worth waiting for.

look.photo: Bold, full-bleed, portrait. The putter head on the green at address, low sun raking across the gold and the white grip, the ball and the hole in soft focus beyond. Shot from the golfer's eyeline so the alignment reads.
look.headline: It gets noticed on every green you walk onto
paras: Putters are the one club everyone in the group sees you use, eighteen times a round, standing still, from four feet away. Most of them are gray. This one is gold and white, and the reviews are close to unanimous about what happens next.

That isn't the reason to buy it. The stroke is. But of every club in the bag, this is the one where looking down at something you actually like is worth the most, because you are looking down at it more than anything else you own.
look.aside: Everyone else is carrying the same putter with someone else's name on it. It's better to be lucky.

quote.q: Putter is well balanced and the weight is perfect. I switched from a blade style and it took a few rounds to get comfortable. Now I have the feel at all distances.

_pricing: The 'it costs $X because we sell direct' paragraph was removed 2026-07-31 (Cole). The price argument is made once, on the homepage's Why Lucky, and repeating it in the product description is the brochure voice.
_club: Takomo-shaped 2026-08-19, matching the Gold, the Black and the Blade: two-beat headline, ONE intro paragraph, two labelled sub-blocks, then the bullets. The sub-blocks reuse `clubGrinds` — see the note in lgp01-gold.json. The three old paragraphs were good and their arguments all survive; they are now shaped so somebody scanning gets the two that decide the purchase (the neck and the grip) without reading the prose.

clubGrinds.k: The neck: it works with your arc
clubGrinds.v: The plumber neck gives the head a slight toe hang, so it swings on the arc your stroke already has rather than asking you to putt straighter than you do. The weight sits out at the edges of the head, and that is what keeps a strike off the toe on its line instead of leaking away.

It arrives with the oversized 3.0 in white and gold already on it, and that is not a small detail. A fat grip takes the wrists out of the stroke, and the wrists are what turn a four-footer into a five-footer coming back. Reviewers mention it more than anything else on the club.

The widget prints "Based on 58 reviews" under the score either way, so nothing is hidden; it just is not the headline. The Blade keeps its count at 147 and the Gold keeps 551.
